area: Headquarters capacity / "expansion" / upgrade concept — what limits how many manager roles/plans an HQ holds, and what "expanding the HQ" can concretely mean for the Store Manager mod
findings:
SHORT ANSWER: there is NO HQ level, tier, size-upgrade, desk-cap or manager-cap mechanic in Big Ambitions. An HQ is just a rented office building running the `ba:businesstype_headquarters` business type. The only thing that "scales with the HQ" is the physical floor area (`BuildingSizeData.squareMeters`), which (a) sets how many desk items must/can be placed and (b) drives by-sqm business requirements. The number of HR/Pricing/Logistics/Purchasing/Headhunter *plans* is completely uncapped. The real limiter on how many managers actually work is the number of assignable desk workstations physically placed in the HQ, one manager per desk per shift.

===============================================================
1. IS THERE AN HQ LEVEL / SIZE / UPGRADE MECHANIC?
===============================================================
No level, no tier, no in-place upgrade. Confirmed by absence: grep for ExpandBuilding|MergeBuilding|CombineBuilding|ChangeBuildingSize|SetBuildingSize|officeLevel|buildingLevel|hqLevel across the whole decomp returns nothing usable (only blueprint-filter helpers).

- `Buildings/Building.cs` (ScriptableObject, one per address): fields `string BuildingSize`, `int BuildingVersion = 1`, `string BuildingType`, `int totalSqm`, `float customMarketPrice`. All immutable at runtime. `BuildingVersion` is only a layout/blueprint variant (see `BuildingSizeData.buildingVersions`, `BuildingSizeInfo`, `BlueprintCreatorUI.LoadBuildingVersions`) — it is NOT a player-facing upgrade.
- `BuildingSizeData.cs`: `int squareMeters`, `BuildingVersion[] buildingVersions`, `CustomerCapacity[] customerCapacities`, `int numberOfVehicleSlots`, `numberOfEntrances`, `wallHeights`. Loaded via `AddressableLoader.Register<BuildingSizeData>("BuildingSizes", BuildingSizeHelper.OnBuildingSizesLoaded)`. Read-only.
- To get a bigger HQ the player rents a different, larger office building and re-establishes the HQ there (or runs a second HQ). There is no "annex the next unit" / "add a floor" system.

HOW AN HQ COMES INTO EXISTENCE (`BizManSettings.cs` ~line 101, and research doc 02):
- Rent a building whose `BuildingType` == `BusinessType("ba:businesstype_headquarters").suitableBuildingType`. HQ's suitable building type is an office (`ba:buildingtype_office`; `BusinessType.suitableBuildingType` is a single string, `BusinessType.cs:20`).
- BizMan → Settings tab → Business Type dropdown (filtered to `BusinessTypeHelper.GetAllPlayerAvailableBusinesses().Where(x => x.suitableBuildingType == building.BuildingType)`) → pick Headquarters → name it → Save. Adds happiness modifier `ba:happinessmodifier_started_a_headquarters`.
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan/HeadquartersList.cs`: `Load()` lists every `BuildingRegistration` where `RentedByPlayer && businessTypeName == "ba:businesstype_headquarters"` — a `FindAll`, so MULTIPLE HQs are allowed; there is no "one HQ per city/save" cap.
- `BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs()` (`BizManBusiness.cs:222-231`) hardcodes the HQ tab set: Presentation, Schedule, PricingManagers, LogisticsManagers, PurchasingAgents, HRManagers, Headhunters, Settings — only when `businessTypeName == "ba:businesstype_headquarters" && RentedByPlayer`.

WHAT SQUARE METERS ACTUALLY DRIVES (`BuildingSizeHelper.GetData(registration).squareMeters`):
- Rent (`Building.GetBuildingDailyMarketRent`), security decay (`BusinessSecurityHelper` `sqm/500`), marketing reach (`BuildingRegistration.cs:530`), customer capacity (n/a for HQ).
- Business-requirement item counts: `SpecificItemsInBuildingBySqm` / `ItemsOfTypeInBuildingBySqm` compute `count = ceil(squareMeters / squareMetersPerItem)`, then `min(count, maxItems)` when `maxItems > 0`. `BizManBusiness.LoadRequirements()` renders these from `BusinessType.businessRequirements`. This is the ONLY "HQ scales with size" behaviour in vanilla, and it is a MINIMUM (you must own at least N office-workstation items), plus an optional hard `maxItems` ceiling on that requirement — not a cap on total desks or managers.

===============================================================
2. IS THERE A CAP ON THE NUMBER OF MANAGER PLANS PER HQ? — NO
===============================================================
Every "add plan" path is unconditional. No cap check, no desk gate, no money gate, and the "+ add plan" row (`buttonEntry`) is always visible/enabled.
- `HrManagersPlanList.AddPlan()` (`UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HrManagers/HrManagersPlanList.cs:292`): `new HrManagerPlan { headquartersAddress = hqAddr }` → `SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans.Add(...)`.
- `PricingManagersPlanList.AddPlan()` (`.../PricingManagers/PricingManagersPlanList.cs:63`): `PricingManagerHelper.AddPlan(new PricingManagerPlan{...})`.
- `PurchasingAgentsPlanList` — the "plan" is `Entities.ImportPartnership` added to `SaveGameManager.Current.importPartnerships`.
- Logistics + Headhunters follow the identical shape.
- Plans are stored in flat `List<T>` on `GameInstance`: `hrManagerPlans`, `pricingManagerPlans`, `logisticsManagerPlans`, `headhunterPlans`, `importPartnerships`. Per-HQ view is just `helper.GetAssignedPlansForHeadquarters(Address)` = `list.Where(x => x.headquartersAddress == address)` (`HrManagerHelper.cs:30`, `LogisticsManagerHelper.cs:56`, `PurchasingAgentHelper.cs:14`, etc.). `BusinessHelper.DeleteHQPlans` (`BusinessHelper.cs:984`) tears them all down when the HQ is shut down.

Per-PLAN caps exist but are SKILL-driven, not HQ-driven:
- `HrManagerPlan.MaxEmployees => HrManagerSkillValue.CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees()` and `HrManagerHelper.CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees(this float skill) => 10 + Mathf.FloorToInt(skill / 5f / 5f) * 10` (i.e. `10 + floor(skill/25)*10`).
- `LogisticsManagerPlan.CalculateMaxDestinations(address, employeeId)` — skill → store cap (casts registration to `Warehouse`; irrelevant to a custom role).
- These are computed from the assigned manager's skill value, nothing about the HQ building.

===============================================================
3. PHYSICAL DESK / WORKSTATION — YES, AND ITS COUNT IS THE REAL LIMITER
===============================================================
An HQ manager occupies an assignable workstation item exactly like a shop cashier occupies a register.

- A plan only counts a manager if that manager is (a) hired, (b) `EmployeeInstance.assignedAddress == hqAddress`, (c) `EmployeeInstance.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()`. The "assign manager" dropdown in every plan list filters with the same predicate, e.g. `HrManagersPlanList.UpdateHrManagerDropdownForPlan`: `x.assignedAddress == HQ && x.HasSkill("ba:skill_hrmanager") && !SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans.Exists(y => y.id != plan.id && y.assignedEmployeeId == x.id) && x.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()`. (Pricing: `PricingManagersPlanList.cs:179`; Purchasing: `PurchasingAgentsPlanList.cs:111`.)
- `ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans()` (`.../Schedule/ScheduleHelper.cs:412-454`) runs on every HQ schedule change and auto-unassigns a manager from its plan the moment it has no work shift (`if (instance != null && !instance.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()) plan.UnAssignEmployee()`), for all five plan types.

- Where the desks come from: `ScheduleHelper.FetchWorkstations()` (`ScheduleHelper.cs:501`) → `BuildingRegistration.GetAssignableItems()` (`BuildingRegistration.cs:584`). That returns every `itemInstance` whose `ItemCached.assignable == true` AND whose `suitableSkills` array intersects `BusinessTypeHelper.GetData(businessTypeName).employeePrimarySkills` ∪ `BuildingTypeHelper.GetData(buildingType).requiredBuildingSkills`.
- The desk items at an HQ are `ba:itemname_desktopcomputer` / `ba:itemname_laptop` / `ba:itemname_computer` (component `Controllers/DesktopWorkstationController.cs : EmployeeStationController` — the employee sits in `employeeChair` and plays a typing animation). Legacy id map also has `ba:itemname_officedesk1/2`, `ba:itemname_desktopworkstation1/2`, `ba:itemname_storemanagerdesk` (id 304), `ba:itemname_specialemployeedesk` (id 301) — `storemanagerdesk`/`specialemployeedesk` are used by `SpecialEmployeeController` for the wholesale/import special employees, not the HQ manager tabs.
- VERIFIED IN-GAME (mod's own probe, 2026-09-02, "Foundation Headquarters" save, in `docs/DESIGN-v2.md:150`): `ba:itemname_desktopcomputer` / `laptop` / `computer` at the HQ list `ba:skill_purchasingagent` in `suitableSkills`, and a skill-100 Purchasing Agent could be scheduled there. The earlier reflection dump indicated all five manager skills sit in that same `suitableSkills` list — i.e. one desk model serves every manager role. (The "all five" part is not re-confirmed by the 2026-09-02 probe; only `ba:skill_purchasingagent` was directly dumped.)
- One employee per workstation per hour. `ScheduleHelper.CalculateEndingHour` + the `IsHeadquarters` branches force an HQ shift to span the whole opening-hour slot (a manager works a full day, `WorkShiftDrag.cs:147`, `WorkShiftSliderHandle.cs:41`), and the HQ is always "open" (`ScheduleHourToggle.cs:72` blocks toggling). So: number of managers that can be scheduled simultaneously == number of assignable desk items placed in the HQ.
- Desk count is bounded by: physical floor space in the Interior Designer, furniture cost, and any `maxItems` on the HQ's by-sqm office-workstation requirement — NOT by a "manager capacity" number. There is no vanilla concept of "this HQ supports N managers".

- SKILL ENFORCEMENT ON SCHEDULING: `ScheduleHelper.HasSkillForWorkstation(workstationId, employeeId)` (`ScheduleHelper.cs:529`) = "does the employee have ANY skill listed in `workstation.ItemCached.suitableSkills`". Enforced on drop/drag: `WorkShiftDrag.cs:138` → on failure `Notifications.ShowError("bizman_schedule_employee_doesnt_have_required_skill")`, and `ScheduleHelper.IsEmployeeAvailable` (`:157`) short-circuits on it. CONSEQUENCE: a Filiaalmanager / Team Leader carrying only a custom `ba:skill_*` CANNOT be scheduled at a vanilla HQ desk unless that desk's `suitableSkills` array contains the custom skill name.

- WAGE / COST LADDER: `EmployeeHelper.CalculateHourlyWageForSkill(string skillName, float skillValue)` (`Helpers/EmployeeHelper.cs:359`) = `SkillHelper.GetData(skillName).baseHourlyWage * GetSkillWageBoost(skillValue) * employeeHourlySalaryMultiplier`. The per-tier wage (~$16 employee → ~$30 Store Manager) is set by each custom skill's `SkillData.baseHourlyWage`, so it needs its own `SkillData` or a Harmony guard on `SkillHelper.GetData` (the same custom-skill fragility already flagged in the brief).

===============================================================
4. WHAT "EXPANDING THE HQ" CAN CONCRETELY MEAN — RECOMMENDATION
===============================================================
"Expand the Headquarters" has NO vanilla mechanic behind it. Three concrete options:

(a) NOTHING NEEDED for plan storage. Vanilla plan lists are uncapped, and the mod already keeps its own plan blob in `GameInstance.modData` (DECISIONS D9/D10). If the mod does not create real vanilla `*ManagerPlan` entries, there is nothing to cap and nothing to expand at the data layer.

(b) ADD THE CUSTOM SKILLS TO EXISTING HQ DESKS' `suitableSkills` — REQUIRED if the two roles are to be rostered through the vanilla BizMan → HQ → Schedule tab (which the design wants for native feel, and which is what gates the supervision plan via `IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()`). Mechanism: Harmony/reflection to append `"ba:skill_filiaalmanager"` and `"ba:skill_teamleader"` to `ItemsGetter.GetByName("ba:itemname_desktopcomputer" | "ba:itemname_laptop" | "ba:itemname_computer").suitableSkills` after each Addressables load of the "Items" catalog, re-applied on every city load (same lifetime problem as the custom `SkillData` — piggyback the same hook). Because those desks already carry the vanilla manager skills (which ARE in `BusinessType("ba:businesstype_headquarters").employeePrimarySkills`), the desks still pass the `GetAssignableItems()` intersection test, so you do NOT strictly need to mutate `BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills` — but adding the two custom skills there too is cheap insurance and keeps `OfficeBusinessSimulator`/`HeadquartersList` counters consistent.

(c) A MOD-DEFINED CAPACITY THAT SCALES WITH THE HQ — pure mod bookkeeping, and the only thing that makes "expanding the HQ" mean something concrete: compute an allowance from real HQ state, e.g. `storeManagerSlots = 1` (fixed; the Store Manager is the apex, one per HQ) and `teamLeaderSlots = f(HQ office desks)` — either `GetAssignableItems().Count` on the HQ registration, or `1 + floor(BuildingSizeHelper.GetData(hqReg).squareMeters / X)`. Enforce it in the mod's own assign panel; when full, surface "HQ full — rent a larger office or add desks" via `Notifications.Show(NotificationType.Warning, ...)` + the permanent phone Contact, mirroring `LogisticsManagerPlan`'s `logistics_alerts` alert pattern. This reuses the game's own "by sqm" idiom.

RECOMMENDATION: combine (b) + (c), and explicitly REJECT any fake building-upgrade button.
- (b) is mandatory plumbing — without the custom skill in the desk `suitableSkills`, the native schedule flow rejects the manager with `bizman_schedule_employee_doesnt_have_required_skill`.
- (c) is the "expansion" design — "expand the HQ" = the player physically rents a bigger office and/or places more desk items, and the mod reads that state (`squareMeters` and/or desk count) to allow more Team Leaders. Model it as: 1 Store Manager per HQ, N Team Leaders where N grows with HQ desks/sqm; the Store Manager approves buying, Team Leaders raise per-department stock requests (departments are mod-invented groupings of stores/product categories, unchanged from the brief).
- Do NOT synthesize a building-size/level change. There is no `BuildingSize` mutation path; faking one would desync rent, security, marketing and business requirements, and there is no ModAPI for it (`BAModAPI/ModdingAPI.cs` only exposes `RegisterModBusinessType` and `RegisterModVehicleType` — no mod-item, no mod-skill, no mod-buildingsize).

keyTypes.name: Buildings.Building
keyTypes.note: ScriptableObject, one per address. Fields BuildingSize/BuildingVersion/BuildingType/totalSqm are fixed at runtime. No upgrade/expand method. BuildingVersion is a layout variant only. This is why 'expanding the HQ' has no vanilla hook.

keyTypes.name: BuildingSizeData
keyTypes.note: int squareMeters, BuildingVersion[] buildingVersions, CustomerCapacity[], numberOfVehicleSlots. Loaded read-only via AddressableLoader Register<BuildingSizeData>("BuildingSizes"). squareMeters is the only thing that 'scales' an HQ.

keyTypes.name: Buildings.BuildingTypes.Shared.BusinessRequirement.SpecificItemsInBuildingBySqm
keyTypes.note: GetRequiredItemCount = ceil(squareMeters / squareMetersPerItem), capped at maxItems. Sibling ItemsOfTypeInBuildingBySqm is identical for an ItemType. This is the game's 'by sqm' idiom the mod's HQ capacity should imitate. MINIMUM requirement + optional maxItems ceiling, not a manager cap.

keyTypes.name: UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HeadquartersList
keyTypes.note: Load(): FindAll(RentedByPlayer && businessTypeName=="ba:businesstype_headquarters") -> multiple HQs allowed, no per-save cap. Per-row counters are hardcoded to 5 skills (pricingmanager/logisticsmanager/purchasingagent/hrmanager/headhunter); a 6th/7th counter row would need Harmony + prefab work.

keyTypes.name: BizManBusiness
keyTypes.note: SetUpTabs() lines 222-231 hardcode the HQ tab list. SetInitialTab hardcodes HQ->PricingManagers. A native-looking mod tab needs Harmony on SetUpTabs+SetTab+Awake plus a GameObject under `containers`.

keyTypes.name: UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HrManagers.HrManagersPlanList
keyTypes.note: AddPlan() (line 292): unconditional new HrManagerPlan -> SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans.Add. NO cap, NO desk gate, '+ add' button always enabled. Manager dropdown filter: assignedAddress==HQ && HasSkill("ba:skill_hrmanager") && !boundElsewhere && IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift().

keyTypes.name: Buildings.Office.Headquarters.HrManagerHelper
keyTypes.note: GetAssignedPlansForHeadquarters(Address) = hrManagerPlans.Where(x.headquartersAddress==address). CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees(this float skill) => 10 + floor(skill/25)*10 — a per-plan cap driven by SKILL, not by the HQ. Same helper shape for Pricing/Logistics/Purchasing/Headhunter.

keyTypes.name: Buildings.Office.Headquarters.HrManagerPlan
keyTypes.note: Plain class in SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans. MaxEmployees => HrManagerSkillValue.CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees(). No reference to building size or desk count.

keyTypes.name: UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.Schedule.ScheduleHelper
keyTypes.note: FetchWorkstations() (line 501) -> BuildingRegistration.GetAssignableItems(). HasSkillForWorkstation(wsId,empId) (line 529) = employee has ANY skill in workstation.ItemCached.suitableSkills. UpdateHQPlans() (line 412) auto-unassigns a manager from its plan when it loses all work shifts. IsHeadquarters (line 37). HQ shifts forced to full opening slot.

keyTypes.name: BuildingRegistration.GetAssignableItems
keyTypes.note: ~line 584: returns itemInstances where ItemCached.assignable && suitableSkills intersects (BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills U BuildingTypeData.requiredBuildingSkills). This is the gate that decides which desks show up in the HQ schedule. A custom-skill role needs a desk whose suitableSkills contains the custom skill AND that still intersects this combined list (vanilla HQ desks already do, via the existing manager skills).

keyTypes.name: Controllers.DesktopWorkstationController
keyTypes.note: EmployeeStationController subclass for the HQ desk (ba:itemname_desktopcomputer / laptop / computer). Employee sits in employeeChair, typing anim. One employee per station.

keyTypes.name: UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.Schedule.WorkShiftDrag
keyTypes.note: Line 138: if (!ScheduleHelper.HasSkillForWorkstation(...)) Notifications.ShowError("bizman_schedule_employee_doesnt_have_required_skill"). This is the wall a custom-skill manager hits at a vanilla desk unless the desk's suitableSkills is patched.

keyTypes.name: BusinessType
keyTypes.note: string suitableBuildingType (single string), string[] employeePrimarySkills. ScriptableObject loaded via Addressables (asset data not in decomp). For HQ, employeePrimarySkills holds the 5 manager skills; adding the 2 custom skills here (Harmony/reflection, re-inject per load) is optional insurance.

keyTypes.name: BuildingTypeData
keyTypes.note: string[] requiredBuildingSkills. For ba:buildingtype_office this feeds the GetAssignableItems() skill union alongside employeePrimarySkills.

keyTypes.name: Helpers.EmployeeHelper.CalculateHourlyWageForSkill
keyTypes.note: Line 359: baseHourlyWage from SkillHelper.GetData(skillName) * GetSkillWageBoost(value) * multiplier. The per-tier cost ladder (~$16 -> ~$30/hr) is set by each custom skill's SkillData.baseHourlyWage; needs a SkillData or a Harmony guard on SkillHelper.GetData.

keyTypes.name: BAModAPI.ModdingAPI
keyTypes.note: Only RegisterModBusinessType(BusinessType) and RegisterModVehicleType(VehicleType). NO mod-item API, NO mod-skill API, NO mod-buildingsize API. A dedicated new HQ desk model or a real building-size change is not reachable through the ModAPI.

keyTypes.name: BizManSettings
keyTypes.note: ~line 101: HQ establish gate. businessTypeDropdown = GetAllPlayerAvailableBusinesses().Where(suitableBuildingType == building.BuildingType). Any rented office of the right building type can become an HQ; establishing is free-form, no size threshold.

keyTypes.name: Helpers.BusinessHelper.DeleteHQPlans
keyTypes.note: ~line 984: on HQ shutdown, deletes all importPartnerships / logisticsManagerPlans / headhunterPlans / hrManagerPlans / pricingManagerPlans whose headquartersAddress == the HQ. Confirms plans are keyed only by HQ address, stored in flat GameInstance lists.

feasibility: MIXED. (1) Plan-count / "capacity" side = NATIVE, nothing to build: vanilla plan lists are uncapped and the mod keeps its own plan blob in modData; any capacity limit is pure mod bookkeeping (read BuildingSizeHelper.GetData(hqReg).squareMeters and/or GetAssignableItems().Count, enforce in the mod's own assign UI). (2) Rostering a custom-skill Filiaalmanager/Team Leader through the vanilla HQ Schedule tab = NEEDS HARMONY: postfix the "Items" Addressables load (AddressableLoader / SkillHelper-style hook) to append "ba:skill_filiaalmanager" / "ba:skill_teamleader" to ItemsGetter.GetByName("ba:itemname_desktopcomputer"|"ba:itemname_laptop"|"ba:itemname_computer").suitableSkills, re-applied on every city load; optionally also reflect the two skills into BusinessType("ba:businesstype_headquarters").employeePrimarySkills. Without this, ScheduleHelper.HasSkillForWorkstation rejects the manager (WorkShiftDrag error bizman_schedule_employee_doesnt_have_required_skill). (3) A dedicated NEW HQ desk model = NEEDS ASSET BUNDLE (no mod-item API). (4) In-place HQ level/size/expand button = INFEASIBLE and should not be attempted — no BuildingSize mutation exists, faking it desyncs rent/security/requirements, and BAModAPI exposes no buildingsize/item/skill registration. "Expanding the HQ" should mean: player rents a bigger office and/or places more desks; the mod reads that state to allow more Team Leaders.
openQuestions: Exact contents of BusinessType("ba:businesstype_headquarters").employeePrimarySkills and its businessRequirements list, and BuildingTypeData("ba:buildingtype_office").requiredBuildingSkills — these are Addressables asset data not present in the decomp. Needs an in-game reflection dump: does the HQ have a SpecificItemsInBuildingBySqm / ItemsOfTypeInBuildingBySqm requirement for office workstations, what squareMetersPerItem and maxItems, and does employeePrimarySkills already contain all 5 manager skills or just some?

Re-confirm in-game which exact desk item ids at an HQ are assignable and what their full suitableSkills arrays are. The 2026-09-02 probe verified ba:itemname_desktopcomputer/laptop/computer carry ba:skill_purchasingagent; the 'all 5 manager skills' claim is from an older reflection dump and not re-verified. Also confirm ba:itemname_desktopcomputer.assignable == true.

Whether appending to Item.suitableSkills at runtime (reflection on the string[] loaded by Addressables) is picked up everywhere it matters (ScheduleHelper.HasSkillForWorkstation reads ItemCached.suitableSkills live, so likely yes) and whether the array must be replaced vs mutated in place, and the exact load hook to re-inject on each city load (mirror the custom SkillData re-inject).

Does placing extra ba:itemname_desktopcomputer/laptop items in the HQ via the Interior Designer have any per-building item cap or per-business-requirement maxItems ceiling that would limit desk count (and therefore the mod's Team-Leader capacity formula)?

Confirm SkillData.baseHourlyWage / SkillHelper.GetData behaviour for a custom skill (NPE risk already flagged) so the ~$16->~$30/hr cost ladder can be delivered either via real SkillData or a Harmony guard — this is the tier-cost lever the design needs.

Whether a mod-registered BusinessType (BAModAPI.ModdingAPI.RegisterModBusinessType) could be used to create a distinct 'expanded HQ' business type variant, or whether that just adds an establish-dropdown entry with none of the hardcoded BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs HQ tab wiring (SetUpTabs keys off the literal string "ba:businesstype_headquarters").
